root_cause.text: The condition in `ccu_mix_trigger_fc()` was inverted, causing the function to return early and skip the frequency change trigger when a valid frequency change register exists, instead of when it doesn't exist.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (common->reg_fc)` to `if (!common->reg_fc)` on line 76. The original logic would return 0 (success) when `common->reg_fc` is non-zero (i.e., when a valid register is present), preventing the actual frequency change trigger operation (`ccu_update()`) from executing. The corrected logic returns early only when `common->reg_fc` is NULL/zero (invalid), allowing the frequency change to proceed when the register is valid. This inverted condition caused kernel panics during cpufreq scaling because the frequency change was never actually triggered.
